Reviewing Agent Code

Reviewing code written by an agent requires a different habit than reviewing code from a colleague. The agent rarely makes typos, but it may confidently call an API that does not exist or solve a slightly different problem from the one you described. I start every review by reading the tests, not the implementation, and I ask whether the tests would fail if the feature were broken. Then I check the edges: empty inputs, network failures and concurrent runs. Finally I read the diff for scope creep, since agents like to tidy unrelated files. This order catches most problems within a few minutes and keeps the review focused on behaviour rather than style, which linters already handle well.
